reference.comment: First-party HF Transformers integration: granite_speech5_ctc / granite_speech5_encoder, GraniteSpeech5ForCTC, GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor and GraniteSpeech5Processor ship inside mainline transformers from v5.16 (dumped with 5.17.0). No trust_remote_code - config.json has no auto_map. The dumper mirrors the model card path: AutoProcessor + AutoModelForCTC + model.generate + processor.batch_decode(skip_special_tokens=True). attn_implementation=eager (GraniteSpeech5 sets _supports_flash_attn=False because the Shaw relative-position bias is a float attention mask). The repo ALSO ships stale ctc_conformer remote code (granite_encoder.py, modeling_ctc_conformer.py) using granite-speech-4.x tensor names; it cannot load this checkpoint and is not the reference.

oracle_dtype_comment: Weights ship BF16 and transformers' dtype='auto' would load BF16, but the dumps and the reference WER baseline are both taken at F32. The BF16->F32 upcast is lossless, so these are the shipped weights unchanged, and F32 activations over BF16 weights is exactly the transcribe.cpp compute regime. Measured on jfk: a BF16 forward gives an identical transcript and identical token ids, but tensors differ from F32 by up to 2-3% of p99_abs (enc.block.1.post_ff2 max |diff| = 0.44), which is ~250x the 1e-4 x p99_abs Stage 2 tolerance budget. A BF16 oracle would therefore force blind tolerance widening at Stage 4 and hide real implementation bugs.

frontend.comment: GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor. torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram(sr=16000, n_fft=512, win_length=400, hop_length=160, n_mels=80) at library defaults: power=2.0, Hann PERIODIC, center=True, pad_mode=reflect, f_min=0, f_max=8000, mel_scale=htk, norm=None (UNNORMALIZED triangular filters, not Slaney). win_length=400 != n_fft=512, so the window is zero-padded to 512 inside the STFT. Then clamp_min(1e-10) -> log10 -> per-utterance floor at (global max over BOTH time and mel bins) - 8.0 -> fixed affine x/4 + 1. That normalization is bit-for-bit src/transcribe-mel.cpp's existing per_utterance mode ((x+4)/4); it is a dynamic-range floor, NOT CMVN. Then concat torchaudio.functional.compute_deltas(win_length=3) along the channel axis (80 -> 160) and stack 2 consecutive frames (160 -> 320). FRAMING: mel_frames = n_samples // 160; num_frames = 2*ceil(mel_frames/2); the WAVEFORM is right-padded to (num_frames-1)*160+1 samples; the melspec is sliced to [..., :num_frames]. For even mel_frames this drops one trailing center-pad frame; for odd mel_frames it keeps it. The trailing partial stacking group is VALID, not masked: encoder_frame_counts = ceil(mel_frames/2) equals the emitted frame count (verified valid=550/550 on jfk, 1767/1767 on dots).

tokenizer_summary.comment: GPT-2-style byte-level BPE. No normalizer; ByteLevel pre-tokenizer (add_prefix_space=false) and ByteLevel decoder (add_prefix_space=true). The only added token is <|blank|> at id 0, which is simultaneously the CTC blank and pad_token_id. The model id space is 1:1 with the tokenizer - no offset, no special-token block to strip - so decoding the post-collapse ids directly yields the transcript. tokenizer_config.json declares tokenizer_class=ParakeetTokenizer, but the artifact is byte-level BPE: spaces come from the byte-level round-trip, and a word opens on a raw piece beginning with U+0120 (C4 A0), not the SentencePiece U+2581.

capabilities.comment: Monolingual English encoder-CTC. Word timestamps are in scope by intake sign-off even though upstream does not advertise them: one encoder frame is exactly 80 ms (8 * 160 / 16000) and the greedy collapse yields the emitting frame per surviving token. Upstream publishes benchmarks only as bar-chart images; the single numeric public figure is 5.00% aggregate Open ASR leaderboard WER. Stage 4 and Stage 7 gate against the measured Oracle reference baseline on LibriSpeech test-clean - see reports/wer/granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-REF.test-clean.{jsonl,score.json}.

cases_comment: jfk has mel_frames=1100 (even) and dots has mel_frames=3533 (odd). The two parities are different code paths in the feature extractor: the odd case right-pads the waveform and keeps the trailing center-pad frame, the even case drops it. dots (35.3 s) also spans many more 128-frame attention blocks than jfk (11.0 s).
